notes: Ghana's Harmonised Births and Deaths Registration Platform (HBDRP), the Births & Deaths Registry's third-party integration API hosted by Npontu. The vendor publishes no OpenAPI, but it does publish a Postman collection — the documentation link @openfn/language-ghana-bdr@1.0.0 cites for its rewrite — which is committed verbatim as upstream.json and converted here by hand (the repo's converters cover OpenAPI/Swagger/Discovery only). 'Full' means every request in that collection: 2 auth, 3 birth, 2 death and 1 utility operation, all 8 modelled, plus the 8 documented callback events folded into one CallbackEvent schema (an outbound webhook to the integrator, not an endpoint, so it is not a path). Schemas come from the collection's example responses and its Req/Cond/Opt field tables; because required-ness there is conditional on status (DRAFT saves as-is, COMPLETE validates everything), only the three fields enforced in both modes are marked required and the rest carry the condition in their description. Two honest gaps: the collection ships no successful death response (the sample institution is authorised for birth services only, so both saved examples are 403s), so DeathRecordResponse.api_data is left open rather than guessed; and process_flow / callback_history are documented in prose for the status lookup but absent from its saved example, so they are modelled as optional. The collection's LIVE folder is empty — every request targets the beta host — so bdr.npontu.com is listed as a second server on the strength of the adaptor's error message and the evidence URLs in the examples. Cross-checked against ast.json and the adaptor source: createBirthRecord, the token exchange, the integration test's record lookup and the utility endpoint its unit-test mock intercepts all exist here. Conformance note: openfn-mocker's ghana-bdr guide still posts the pre-1.0.0 nested payload and exposes a GET .../registrations/birth list endpoint the vendor does not document; both are mock-side gaps, not spec gaps, and are left for the mocker to fix.
